key_insight: Reframe video editing from a data-to-data to a noise-to-data process and perform few-step streaming generation, enabling high-quality, temporally consistent edits without additional training.
problem_solved: Current video editing approaches require many costly optimization iterations, struggle to integrate with modern generative (noise-to-data) models, and often sacrifice quality or temporal consistency.
method: Revisit editing as noise-to-data generation and leverage off-the-shelf generative models (no extra training).
Perform streaming (frame-by-frame or chunked) few-step generation that preserves temporal coherence while minimizing per-frame computation.
Steer generation with conditioning (e.g., prompts, masks, reference frames) to apply edits efficiently in a training-free manner.
impact: Offers a fast, low-cost pathway to high-quality video edits that maintain temporal consistency, making advanced video editing practical for researchers and production pipelines without model re-training.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram comparing data-to-data (many iterations) vs. noise-to-data streaming (few-step) workflows.
Before / after frame sequence showing preserved temporal coherence across edited frames.
Bar chart comparing runtime and iteration count vs. perceived quality for StreamGVE and baseline methods.
paper_title: StreamGVE: Training-Free Video Editing via Few-Step Streaming Video Generation
paper_authors: Guanlong Jiao, Chenyangguang Zhang, Jia Jun Cheng Xian, Zewei Zhang, Renjie Liao
